resolutions.researcher_notes: Haradh Gas Plant (which the Tinat sweet-gas gathering line feeds) came on stream April 2003 and was fully online by June 2003; still operating. offshore-technology.com/projects/haradh describes the Tinat manifold and its transmission lines as part of the live plant; wcu.edu PMI case study (BNP04, confirmed via PDF text extraction: 'The plant came to life in April 2003 when the first sweet gas train went on stream. By June 2003 Haradh was fully on line') independently corroborates operating status. url_verifier returned 200 on the wcu PDF but cannot parse PDF text, so the token check was done via local pdfminer extraction. Supports Status=operating.

Both sources confirm this is a natural-gas (sweet gas) system. offshore-technology: 'The Waqr and Tinat manifolds ... carry sweet gas ... The gas is carried to the plant by five 20in and 30in gas transmission lines.' wcu.edu PMI: 'gathering, processing, and distributing sweet, dry sales gas.' Supports Fuel=Gas.

offshore-technology: 'The Waqr and Tinat manifolds are located 50km and 44km, respectively, from the plant.' The Tinat manifold at 44 km from the Haradh plant corroborates GEM's 43.00 km within ~1 km (rounding of the gathering-line run). MINOR DISCREPANCY to flag: source says 44 km vs GEM 43.00 km. Only one source gives the Tinat-specific distance, so medium. (wcu PMI gives only aggregate network figures '680 km of pipelines' / '755 km of 18 to 56 inch pipelines', not this segment.)

offshore-technology: 'The gas is carried to the plant by five 20in and 30in gas transmission lines that total 130km.' 20 in is one of the two stated diameters for the Waqr/Tinat gathering lines, corroborating GEM's Diameter=20 in. wcu PMI's '18 to 56 inch' range is consistent but not segment-specific. Single specific source → medium.

Tinat manifold and Haradh gas plant are in the South Ghawar field region of eastern Saudi Arabia. offshore-technology places the Haradh project (Tinat/Waqr manifolds) in Saudi Arabia; wcu PMI: 'wells in South Ghawar ... Saudi Aramco'. Both endpoints in Saudi Arabia. Supports Start/EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Aramco developed, owns and operates the Haradh Gas Program including the Tinat gathering system. offshore-technology names Saudi Aramco as the operator/supplier; wcu PMI repeatedly attributes the program to 'Saudi Aramco' ('accelerated the development of Saudi Aramco's resources of non-associated gas'). Supports Owner1=Saudi Aramco 100%.
